text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
POLITICAL FRONT PAGE NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati appealed to political parties not to use the issue of Poland's planned entry to NATO for their political goals during the parliamentary elections campaign this summer.
- Free trade agreement between Poland and Turkey will be implemented in January 1998, Turkey's President Suleyman Demirel said during his visit to Warsaw yesterday.
ECONOMIC AND FRONT PAGE NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's poultry producers, which account for about 13 percent of Polish farms, are better adjusted to the EU standards than producers in other agricultural sectors.
- Kredyt Bank is planning to buy a controlling stake in the Lithuanian Litimpeks bank in a consortium with the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development, Kredyt Bank said.
- BRE Services leasing branch of the listed Export Development Bank (BRE) is in talks with a Western concern on an industrial plant lease in Poland worth $13.8 million.
- IBCA experts will come to Poland next week to examine the country's credit rating. IBCA now rates Poland BBB.
- Poland's agricultural market agency (ARR), the government's food market regulator, will buy 100,000 tonnes of consumption wheat from the 1996 crops, the agency said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- An agreement on restructuring the ailing Gdynia shipyard, due to be signed between the treasury ministry and the Szczecin shipyard (SS), will give SS control of the Gdynia yard, the treasury ministry said.

- Mercedes Benz Polska controlled by Mercedes Benz and Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum has presented the new Actros truck model assembled in the Jelcz plant. Around 500 Actros trucks will roll off the Jelcz assembly lines by the end of 1997.

- Toyota will decide on the location of its new plant in Europe in the second half of 1998, the concern's president Hiroshi Okuda said. By that time it may prove impossible to locate it in the area of the Katowice Special Economic Zone in southern Poland as several other concerns have already applied to set up their plants in the zone, the zone's management said.
- Around 200 construction sector firms are exhibiting their products at the Fourth Construction Forum Fairin Bialystok, north-eastern Poland.
- Poland's chocolate output was 15,000 tonnes in the first quarter of 1997, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- The revenues of seven biggest public relations firms in Poland reached $5 million in the first three quarters of 1996. "The market is developing at an intensive rate and the number of customers and contracts grows", Jerzy Ciszewski of Ciszewski PR said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Polfa Kutno pharmaceutical plant has sold a vitamin and mineral salt plant to Germany's BASF concern. The firms refused to disclose the value of the contract prior to Polfa's general shareholders meeting on June 16.

- Individuals have acquired around around 560,000 life insurance policies from the PZU Zycie (Life) insurer, which gives the company a leading position in the life policy market, PZU Zycie's president Wladyslaw Jamrozy said.
ZYCIE
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is planning to buy 847,000 N-series shares of Kredyt Bank, which will give EBRD a 7.8 percent stake in the bank.
PARKIET

- Warta insurance firm's gross premium in the first quarter of 1997 grew by 33 percent compared with the same period last year while Polisa insurance firm has reported a 50 percent gross premium upturn in the same period.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
